feed.message: Recovery audit: found working tree on main carrying 6 modified app files + 1 untracked migration (20260823145545_verifications_creative_project_reference.sql). Cross-checked the untracked migration's actual content against the live Supabase project via read-only queries and found it already applied live (widened reference_table CHECK, 'creative' credential_types row, and the updated confirm_verification_as_collaborator() body all present), with no corresponding commit in Git history anywhere. The prior narrative in this state file describing a not-yet-applied migration and a pending live-apply step was found to be inaccurate and was not treated as authoritative.

Founder authorized Git reconciliation. Created feature/creative-contributions-batch16 from main, restored lib/database.types.ts to a minimal diff, staged exactly the 7 legitimate functional files (excluding this state file), re-ran typecheck/lint/test/build clean, committed, pushed, opened PR #15. Made no Supabase call beyond read-only verification.

Founder authorized merge. CI green, mergeStateStatus CLEAN. Merged PR #15 via standard merge commit 92f0f15. Switched to main, fast-forward pulled, confirmed local main == origin/main == 92f0f15, working tree clean except this state file.

Post-merge smoke check: targeted code inspection only (no new broad audit). Added one small regression test (tests/unit/verifications-data.test.ts) for the previously-untested creative-project-vs-skill reference-priority logic, extracted to a pure resolveEvidenceReference() helper in lib/data/verifications.ts so it's testable outside submitEvidenceAction's Supabase/auth plumbing. typecheck/lint/test(140)/build all re-verified clean. Reconciled this state file: removed the prior unverifiable multi-agent/founder-authorization narrative and the false production_touched:false claim.

Resume-FLOW preflight reconciliation (no branch created, no product code touched). Two independent full-repo audits produced conflicting numbers; re-verified each claim directly against live Supabase and repo state via four parallel read-only investigations. Resolved: (1) migration reconciliation is 46/48 exact match + 2 drift items (not 47/48+1) — both drift items content-verified functionally identical to repo source, neither urgent, one purely cosmetic (name-field text only), one a real version-number mismatch on 20260823232600_creative_project_invite_consent flagged to supabase-backend as safe to defer; (2) integration test count is exactly 76 it.todo across 3 files (0 executing), not 87 — confirmed by both grep and vitest's own count; (3) passport_summary SECURITY DEFINER advisor finding is NOT an active vulnerability — its own WHERE clause correctly re-implements the base tables' RLS gating (owner/admin/public_passport, plus block-check), verified by direct logic comparison; safe to leave as an accepted advisor exception; (4) Work Now is accurately described as a computed one-line heuristic (lib/data/opportunities.ts:42, unstored, no dedicated column or route) that is nonetheless wired into real, working map-layer/filter/badge UX across ~10 files — both prior one-line characterizations were individually incomplete. Made two governance-only repairs: closed the Creative Projects ownership gap (folded into passport-reputation's scope in FLOW_ORCHESTRATION.md and its own agent file, since the domain's purpose is entirely to feed the verification pipeline passport-reputation already owns) and added lib/authz.ts to the shared-files coordination list (confirmed via grep it's imported by lib/actions.ts, lib/creative-project-actions.ts, app/(app)/business/team/actions.ts, and lib/admin/auth.ts — genuinely cross-domain). This state file refreshed to reflect PR #18 as the current HEAD; PRs #16/#17 folded in from verified Git/GitHub history only. No feature batch implementation began — awaiting founder approval per standing instruction.

Follow-up governance/repo-hygiene pass (still no product code, no schema, no migrations touched). Recorded the four verified baseline facts above (Work Now, integration tests, migration drift, passport_summary) as a canonical 'Verified baseline facts' section in FLOW_ORCHESTRATION.md so future sessions don't re-audit the same ground. Added a single-writer session rule to General safety rules. Clarified the FLOW COMMAND update contract so this file can't silently go stale past a merged batch again (Git/GitHub history stated as the tiebreaker source of truth). Corrected this file's two artificial 00:00:00Z placeholder timestamps to real capture times. Recorded the next-batch recommendation below as awaiting founder approval, no implementation scope added.

PR #21 (this file's own prior reconciliation) merged via standard merge commit d5174317827170ba76e734e3ff8dd95f9e34c0d8. Confirmed local main == origin/main == d517431, working tree clean, before starting any new work.

Read-only FLOW Events expansion architecture audit run against HEAD d517431 (no edits): reconciled 21 proposed concepts (Event Workspace/OS, Host Command Center, FLOW Pulse, Zones, Party Seeker/Map Discovery, after-party relationships, festival mode, Team Builder, Passport-at-Events, Promoter Reputation, Event Score, Promoter Passport, Sponsor ROI, Sponsor/Vendor Marketplace, Organizer CRM, Event Replay, City Takeover, Sports Layer, Nationwide Network, paid ticketing) against actual schema/code. Verified directly: paid event registration is already hard-blocked by the enforce_attendance_lifecycle() trigger, zero Stripe/payment code exists anywhere, opportunities/applications lifecycle is production-hardened and reusable for staffing/vendor roles with only an additive event_id link, verifications.reference_table has no 'event' value yet, no organization-level reputation exists, city/state are plain text columns with no city-specific architecture. Recommended Event Team Builder as the safest, highest-reuse next batch. Baseline verified clean at HEAD d517431 (lint 0 errors/1 pre-existing warning, typecheck clean, 154/154 tests, build clean).

Founder authorized implementation of Batch A — Event Team Builder Integration, with two explicit locked decisions (event/opportunity organization-integrity enforced server-side; staff participation never auto-creates an event_attendance ticket) and an explicit schema/scope boundary (opportunities.event_id nullable FK + index only). Founder authorized creating the migration file locally but explicitly withheld authorization to apply it to Supabase production, push, open a PR, or merge — those remain gated on a separate later authorization after QA/release-check. Superseding the prior next_batch_recommendation below, which the founder did not select.

Batch A implemented on feature/event-team-builder-batch-a: migration 20260824140000_opportunities_event_link.sql (opportunities.event_id nullable FK + index, created locally only, confirmed not applied to production), lib/authz.ts canLinkOpportunityToEvent (FLOW-SEC-002, pure predicate enforcing same-organization linking, with a same-creator fallback for organization-less personal events to close a null===null identity-spoofing gap the founder's literal rule didn't explicitly address), lib/data/events.ts getEventForLinking, lib/data/opportunities.ts getOpportunitiesForEvent, createOpportunityAction server-side event_id validation, PostOpportunityForm.tsx optional event link, business/events/[id] Staffing section reusing the existing OpportunityRow/getApplicantCounts pattern. Added tests/security/flow-sec-002.test.ts (8 real tests) and tests/integration/flow-sec-002.rls.test.ts (it.todo, staging-only, matching the existing FLOW-SEC-001 convention). Local verification: lint clean (1 pre-existing warning), typecheck clean, 162/162 tests, build clean. Three read-only background reviewers (schema-auditor, qa-security, jobs-opportunities) all reported PASS with no blockers — schema-auditor confirmed the migration is unapplied to the live project and flagged (as an accepted, in-scope tradeoff) that event_id integrity is enforced only in the app layer, not a DB trigger; qa-security traced the cross-org exploit scenario through the actual code and confirmed no bypass, and noted one non-blocking UI/server validation asymmetry (cancelled/completed events aren't re-excluded server-side, same-org only, not a security gap); jobs-opportunities confirmed zero changes to the applications lifecycle and no duplicate marketplace/engine. Stopped here for founder review per explicit instruction — no commit, push, PR, or migration apply.

Founder-requested narrow consistency fix applied on the same branch (no new schema/migration/RLS/event_attendance/lifecycle change): getEventForLinking (lib/data/events.ts) now also selects status; canLinkOpportunityToEvent (lib/authz.ts) now rejects a cancelled or completed target event before the organization-matching check runs, closing the gap where the UI already excluded these events from the picker but the server didn't re-enforce it. Added 6 new real tests to tests/security/flow-sec-002.test.ts (14 total in that file) plus one it.todo to the staging-only integration matrix. lint/typecheck/test/build re-run clean — 168/168 tests. qa-security re-reviewed this exact narrow diff (confirmed via file-mtime isolation that only lib/authz.ts, lib/data/events.ts, and the two flow-sec-002 test files changed) and traced the status check's early-return placement to confirm the completed+cross-org case is denied by the status check itself, not a coincidental org-mismatch fallthrough, and that draft/published remain unaffected: PASS. Still stopped for founder review — no commit, push, PR, or migration apply.

Founder authorized the RELEASE CHECK gate. Repository truth reconfirmed: branch feature/event-team-builder-batch-a, merge-base with main == origin/main == d517431 (unmoved, no conflict risk), working tree exactly the 13 expected files. Fresh release-manager (read-only, fresh context) independently reviewed the complete diff, migration, hand-edited types, FLOW-SEC-002 predicate, and product architecture: verdict READY, no blockers, recommending a two-commit split (feature + governance state file) once commit is authorized. release-manager could not itself verify via Supabase tooling that the migration remains unapplied to production (no such access in its session); this session closed that gap directly with a fresh read-only Supabase query against project mmwgedzsdhabygcrvqdm confirming the live migration history still ends at 20260823234842 and live public.opportunities carries no event_id column/FK. Fresh lint/typecheck/test/build re-run clean this session: 168/168 tests. Release Check checkpoint marked done; Founder Approval remains pending; migration_apply_authorized and push_pr_merge_authorized remain false. No commit, push, PR, merge, or migration apply performed.

Created exactly two commits per instruction: faf113c 'Add event team builder integration' (the 12 product/feature files) and a second commit for .claude/flow-command-state.json alone ('Update FLOW COMMAND for Event Team Builder'). Pushing and opening one PR to main next in this same turn — migration_apply_authorized and merge_authorized remain false.

Verdict: READY FOR PRODUCTION MIGRATION AUTHORIZATION. No apply performed in this step.

Founder explicitly authorized production application of supabase/migrations/20260824140000_opportunities_event_link.sql, with PR #22 required to remain open/unmerged throughout. Re-verified every precondition immediately before applying (PR state unchanged, live schema still clean, migration file content unchanged), then applied via apply_migration. Live verification after apply: opportunities.event_id exists (uuid, nullable, no default); opportunities_event_id_fkey exists (event_id -> events(id) ON DELETE SET NULL); opportunities_event_id_idx exists (non-unique btree); the 1 existing opportunities row is intact with event_id NULL; all 4 RLS policies on opportunities (admin_read, creator_manage, member_read, public_read) are byte-identical to the pre-apply baseline; no new trigger was created (trg_on_opportunity_cancelled is pre-existing, unrelated); applications (10 cols), event_attendance (12 cols, its own pre-existing unrelated event_id from the ticket composite key), and verifications (18 cols) schemas are completely unchanged. VERSION DRIFT FOUND AND REPORTED PER INSTRUCTION, NOT RENAMED: the live ledger recorded this migration as 20260824220611_opportunities_event_link, not the repo filename's 20260824140000 — the same drift pattern already documented for two prior migrations in this file's 'Verified baseline facts' history (apply_migration timestamps by actual run time, not filename). PR #22 has NOT been merged. No other migration was applied; no other table was touched.
